title: on Windows the ground loop restarts itself through pythonw and a successor, because os.execv does not replace a process there
intention: When its own files change on Windows the ground loop restarts as a windowless successor and the old image exits, so test_heartbeat's restart tooth stops reading red there; off Windows it still re-execs in place.
why: Measured 2026-11-23 on akiendell: test_heartbeat.py's tooth 'a changed own file re-execs the loop in place' reads restarted=False, pid=17112 vs 16876 (and pid=24280 vs 1884 with heartbeat.py unedited), a red that stood before ticket 8c829d9b38b8. os.execv on Windows starts a new process and the old one exits, so the pid cannot stay and the successor runs sys.executable, the venv python.exe launcher (a console, per ticket 8c829d9b38b8's measurement); __main__.py:120 is named in that ticket's why. HYPOTHESIS (Law 3): that execv's successor owns a console is read from the launcher measurement, not yet measured on this path.
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8 (measured, with a proof a hollow build could not pass); outline 10.3.2.1; Akien 2026-11-23 via the orchestrator: akiendell is still throwing up windows as it goes.
how: In __main__.py the restart branch calls a restart helper: off nt os.execv as now; on nt it starts [background_pythonw(), *orig_argv[1:]] detached, releases the run lock, and exits 0 so the successor takes the lock. A red-first proof drives a loop over a scratch home, changes its own file, and reads a new 'started' in beat.json from a pythonw tree with no conhost and no visible console, with the old pid gone.

clauses.claim: on Windows a changed own file leaves a successor loop that writes a new started to beat.json, runs from pythonw with no python.exe, conhost.exe or visible console window in its tree, and the old pid is gone
off Windows the restart is os.execv(sys.executable, orig_argv): the same pid, a new image
COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART still suppresses the restart and COMMAND_EXIT still stops the loop with rc 0, on both

decisions.text: D1: __main__.py gains a restart helper: os.execv off nt, a detached background_pythonw successor plus a clean exit on nt.
D2: the proof drives a loop over a scratch home on the host and reads beat.json and the process tree; one tooth per clause.

D3: test_heartbeat.py's restart tooth reads 'same pid' only where the OS can keep it; on nt it reads a new started and a new live pid. HELD on the question opened at /sorted: the tooth is a spec clause (charter falsifier 2: 're-execing in place') and only his head can say whether a successor is 'in place' on Windows.

measured.saw: visible ConsoleWindowClass windows were venv python3.exe launchers spawned detached (pulse.py, started by heartbeat.spawn_pulses); the same call shape stands in this site's source.
measured.how: EnumWindows poller at 20-40 ms over two runs of about 350 s on akiendell; source read of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/__main__.py
